companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce segment operating profit
companies.metric_basis: Meituan discloses 'Core Local Commerce' (food delivery + Instashopping/Keeta + in-store/hotel/travel) segment operating profit each quarter in its HKEX filings; this line absorbed nearly all delivery-war subsidy costs.

periods.src: HKEX filing/earnings call, reported via Sina Finance/ifeng

companies.latest_signal: Management said Q2 2026 marked a swing back to profit as the industry's subsidy competition became 'more rational,' with Meituan pulling per-order subsidies on low-value orders and pushing price-sensitive users to 'Pinhaofan' instead; but they flagged margins will dip again in H2 2026 as reinvestment resumes and industry subsidy levels remain well above 2024, so normalization will take several more quarters.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: China/Alibaba E-commerce Group adjusted EBITA (official) + Taobao Instant Commerce/Ele.me standalone net loss (sell-side/media estimate, not company-disclosed)
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not break out Taobao Shanggou (Taobao Instant Commerce)/Ele.me losses on their own; the closest official proxy is 'China E-commerce Group' (Taobao & Tmall) adjusted EBITA, which absorbs the quick-commerce subsidy drag. From the June-2026 quarter Alibaba merged this into a broader 'Alibaba E-commerce Group' segment (adding international commerce), breaking clean comparability. Analysts (HSBC, cited by 36Kr/Sina) separately estimate Taobao Shanggou's standalone quarterly net loss.

companies.latest_signal: On the Nov-2025 call management said per-order Shanggou losses had roughly halved versus Jul/Aug 2025 levels as order mix and logistics efficiency improved; by the June-2026 quarter analysts estimate the standalone loss narrowed sharply quarter-on-quarter (per-order loss down to ~RMB3.5 from ~RMB5+), with unit economics 'continuing to improve quarter-over-quarter' per the filing — but Alibaba restructured segment reporting the same quarter (merging in international commerce), clouding trend visibility just as losses seemed to moderate.

periods.src: HKEX filing/earnings call, reported via Sina Finance/Tencent News

companies.latest_signal: CEO Sandy Xu told the Q2 2026 call that profit growth was driven by both core retail margin expansion and continued delivery loss-narrowing, crediting more refined subsidy targeting (lower per-order subsidy) and rising delivery efficiency as order volume scales; unit-economics for delivery have 'clearly optimized' one year post-launch even as order volumes keep growing.

war_summary: The three platforms have burned an estimated RMB150-220bn combined since the war began in early 2025 (HSBC estimated ~RMB173bn for Meituan+Alibaba+JD in the trailing four quarters through Q1 2026 alone), but Q3 2025-Q2 2026 earnings calls show a synchronized rhetorical pivot from 'scale/subsidies' to 'efficiency/healthy growth,' reinforced by Beijing's anti-'involution' campaign (SAMR price-competition guidance, talk of a unified national market regulation targeting subsidy wars) that made regulators an explicit third party pressuring de-escalation. Meituan defended its #1 share and flipped its core segment back to profit in Q2 2026; JD reached ~15% delivery share (~2.4bn cumulative users) while cutting new-business losses over 50% YoY; Alibaba's Taobao Shanggou/Ele.me stabilized share near 45% (from ~20% pre-war) via the Ele.me-Shanggou merger but remains the least willing to fully stand down, with management still framing instant commerce as a core strategic pillar into FY2027 even as its per-order losses narrow.
